text:
maria: Heads-up — after today's RBAC schema migration some admins can still see org usage & cost pages despite being removed from the billing_viewer role. Noticed during a support call. :eyes:
kevin: can you repro? which org?
maria: repro on acct redwood-test-42. I removed billing_viewer from role 'support_admin' then logged in as test user — console still shows 'Usage & cost' tab and full per-route metrics.
sam: did the migration touch the role -> permission mapping? I ran the migrate script.
kevin: quick grep shows new permission namespaced as 'analytics.view' but some controllers still check for 'billing_view' legacy perm. suspect permission_aliases table missing entry for billing_view -> analytics.view.
devops-bot: AUDIT_LOG: user=system_migration script=migrate_rbac_v2 status=success changes=roles:124,perm_map:45
olivia: paste the role JSON you used to remove billing_view
maria: pasted:
```
roles:
  - id: support_admin
    permissions: ["users.read", "tickets.manage", "analytics.view"]
```
maria: note we expected to remove 'billing_view' but analytics.view is broader — includes cost insights.
sam: root cause looks like two things: 1) alias mapping for legacy perms wasn't populated, 2) migration accidentally set an 'is_admin' flag on roles matching 'support_*' which grants console-wide admin bypass.
kevin: so alias gap + accidental admin flag = overshared access.
maria: severity? any prod customers impacted?
maria: found in redwood-test-42 and a customer report from acme-ai-prod about unexpected access to cost dashboards.
olivia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback RBAC migration to restore previous perm map; 2) remove any is_admin toggles applied by migration; 3) gate the usage/cost UI behind explicit 'billing_view' perm temporarily; 4) run audit of accesses and notify CS/compliance.
sam: starting rollback now. opening INC-5123 and doing DB rollback for role_flags.
kevin: I'll open a quick PR to change the console check to require explicit 'billing_view' perm (feature-flagged) so rollback window is safe.
maria: @jen can SRE add a temporary ACL on the edge to block /api/v1/usage/details for non-billing roles?
jen: yes. I can add an nginx acl that checks role payload for 'billing_view' and deny otherwise. ETA ~25m.
devops-bot: AUDIT_LOG: action=acl_update user=jen status=queued
olivia: I'll run an audit query for last 24h hits to cost endpoints and collect user ids + orgs, then share with CS and legal if needed.
maria: thanks. Sam/kevin, please add CI tests to catch alias gaps: ensure every legacy perm has a mapping and migration doesn't flip is_admin for non-admin patterns.
sam: adding unit + integration tests now. PR will include a CI guard.
kevin: timeline: rollback in 30m, edge ACL live in 25m, audit results in 2h, CS outreach within 3h.
maria: tagging @cs-leads and @compliance. cc @oncall.
olivia: I'll draft a short incident note and send to incident-ops with root cause and mitigation steps.
maria: keep this thread updated, thanks everyone.
